summary: Arthur Anthony Macdonell worked in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Göttingen, Oxford, and Leipzig under Theodor Benfey, Friedrich Max Müller, and Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at Oxford, including Boden Professor of Sanskrit (1880–1899) and Deputy Professor (~1888–1899).

Arthur Berriedale Keith was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at the University of Edinburgh under Julius Eggeling and at Balliol College, Oxford, under Arthur Anthony Macdonell. He served in the Colonial Office (~1901–1914) and taught at Edinburgh (1914–1944).

Arthur Christensen worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Copenhagen under Johannes Edvard Lehmann and Michael Viggo Fausbøll, and under Friedrich Carl Andreas. He served as docent at the University of Copenhagen (1919–1945).

Arthur Coke Burnell was an Indologist and linguist. He studied at King's College London under Theodor Goldstücker, as well as under Michael Viggo Fausbøll and Heinrich August Jäschke. In 1860 he joined the Indian Civil Service.
Arthur Evans was an archaeologist and historian. He was educated at Harrow School and studied at Brasenose College, Oxford, in 1870.
Arthur F. Buehler works in religious studies and Indology. He studied under Annemarie Schimmel and held a post at Victoria University of Wellington.

Arthur F. Wright worked in Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Stanford, Oxford, and Harvard under John King Fairbank. He served on the faculty at Stanford (1947, 1958) and as Professor of History at Yale (1959, 1961).
Arthur Galletti worked in linguistics and Indology. He studied at Cheltenham College and Trinity College, Oxford. From 1900 to 1934, he served as a civil servant in the Indian Civil Service.
Arthur Haberlandt worked in history and archaeology. He held a post at the University of Vienna from ~1914 to 1945.

Arthur Henry Ewing worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Washington & Jefferson College, Pittsburgh Theological Seminary, and Johns Hopkins. He served as director of Christian Boys' Boarding School (1891–1898) and president of Ewing Christian College (1898–1909).

Arthur Henry Fox Strangways worked in Indology. He studied Classics at Balliol College, Oxford, and at the Berlin University of the Arts. He worked as a schoolmaster at Dulwich College (1884–1886) and Wellington College (1886–1910).
Arthur James Beattie was a linguist. He was educated at Montrose Academy and studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1931–1935) and the University of Cambridge (~1935–1937).

Arthur Leslie Saunders worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Balliol College, Oxford (~1880–1882), joined the Indian Civil Service in 1880, and served at the India Office from 1918 to 1923.

Arthur Llewellyn Basham was an Indologist and historian. He studied at SOAS under Lionel David Barnett. His main posts included professor at SOAS (1957–1965) and Head of the Department of Asian Civilizations at the Australian National University (1965–1979).
Arthur Marshman Spencer was an Indologist. He was educated at Kingswood School and studied at Headingley College (~1907–1910).
Arthur Mason Tippetts Jackson worked in Indology and history. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1884–1888) and served in the Indian Civil Service from ~1888 to 1909.

Arthur Maurice Hocart was an archaeologist and Indologist. He studied at Exeter College, Oxford. He served as Sri Lanka's Archaeological Commissioner (1921–1929), lecturer at University College London (1931–1934), and professor of sociology at Cairo University (1934).

Arthur Philip McKeown specializes in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at Harvard University (attested 2005), where he studied under Parimal G. Patil, Pari Sangye, and Diana L. Eck.

Arthur Schopenhauer was a philosopher who studied at Göttingen, Berlin (under Friedrich Schleiermacher, August Boeckh, and Friedrich August Wolf), and Jena. He also attended lectures by Friedrich Majer and held a lectureship at the Humboldt University of Berlin in 1820.

Arthur Venis was an Indologist who studied at the University of Edinburgh and Balliol College, Oxford. He was principal at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University across multiple terms between 1885 and 1914, and became Professor of Post-Vedic Sanskrit at Allahabad (1914–1918).
